title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed announced that SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not publish on Friday, April 3, 2026 due to a market holiday anomaly caused by the March Employment Situation release occurring on Good Friday. EFFR and OBFR will publish on April 3 following the New York Fed's own holiday schedule. The SOFR complex rates will instead publish on Monday, April 6, reflecting repo transactions settling Thursday, April 2.
key_points: SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR Averages/Index will NOT publish on April 3, 2026 due to lack of cleared Treasury repo settlement
EFFR and OBFR WILL publish on April 3, 2026 as they follow the New York Fed's own holiday schedule
SIFMA did not recommend a full market closure for U.S. government securities despite Good Friday
Cleared Treasury repo settlement is not scheduled for April 3, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
On April 6, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will be published reflecting same-day settling repo transactions that settle Thursday April 2 and mature Monday April 6
The SOFR Averages and Index published April 6 will have a value date of April 6
why_it_matters: This notice reveals a specific market infrastructure edge case where Fed reference rate publication schedules differ based on which benchmark is calculated and who administers it. Market participants relying on SOFR-linked instruments, derivatives, or valuation on April 3 should note the unavailability of the overnight benchmark and plan accordingly.
market_structure_context: The notice highlights the dependency of SOFR on cleared Treasury repo settlement availability, with two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates eliminated on April 3. This demonstrates the market plumbing linkages between the employment data release calendar, SIFMA holiday recommendations, cleared repo infrastructure, and reference rate publication schedules.
notes: Source is a direct operating policy notice from the New York Fed. Published March 12, 2026, providing advance notice for April 3 reference rate publication disruption. The notice is relevant to market structure as it describes benchmark rate calculation dependencies on cleared repo settlement infrastructure. The SOFR is the dominant overnight rate benchmark replacing LIBOR, making this a material operational notice for any market participant using SOFR-linked products.
